question: Explain the working principle of a cyclotron without using a diagram. Obtain the expression for cyclotron frequency and show why the frequency is independent of the speed of the charged particle. Hence calculate the cyclotron frequency for a proton in a magnetic field of $0.80\text{ T}$. Given $q=1.6\times10^{-19}\text{ C}$ and $m=1.67\times10^{-27}\text{ kg}$.

options.A: A cyclotron uses a uniform magnetic field for circular motion and an alternating electric field to accelerate the charge across the gap. From $qvB=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$, $T=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ and $\nu=\dfrac{qB}{2\pi m}$, independent of speed. For a proton in $0.80\,\text{T}$, $\nu\approx1.22\times10^7\,\text{Hz}$.
options.B: A cyclotron uses only an electric field. Its frequency is $\nu=\dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ and increases with speed; for a proton it is $8.2\times10^{-8}\,\text{Hz}$.
options.C: The frequency is $\nu=\dfrac{qvB}{2\pi m}$; for a proton it is $1.22\times10^7\,\text{Hz}$ and depends on speed.
options.D: The particle moves in a straight line in the magnetic field; its frequency is $\nu=\dfrac{qB}{m}=7.66\times10^7\,\text{Hz}$.
